subject: Liability limits — IP indemnity trigger, escrow timing, and evidence windows
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie@digicorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@digicorp.com
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carve-out maximum / evidence timing for IP indemnity

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency guarantees. Legal pulled the redlines on the MSA and we have one open commercial point we'd like to resolve before we proceed to signature.

Specifically: Digicorp needs the MSA to preserve the full liability ceiling in cases where Redwood is indemnifying Digicorp for third-party intellectual property infringement (we normally seek unlimited liability for IP indemnities or at least a separate unlimited bucket / royalty remedy). Our contracts team also requires a clear evidence-preservation timeline and a short window to secure injunctive relief if needed.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can: 1) accept an IP-specific exception to the general monetary cap (or provide an alternative remedy such as a royalty % calculation); 2) commit to a defined evidence window (we suggest 30 days after notice) for responses and preservation; and 3) include a short injunctive relief carve-out (no monetary cap on equitable relief).

We'd like to close this before we route to procurement — can you provide proposed language or a counter?

Thanks,
Natalie Park
Senior Contracts Manager — Digicorp
contracts@digicorp.com

Attachment: Digicorp_MSA_Redlines_2028-04-12.docx (redline summary)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Digicorp's ask. TL;DR: They want the IP indemnity excluded from the liability limit (or a royalty alternative), a 30-day evidence-preservation response window, and explicit injunctive relief carve-out. Pricing is already in the order form; sales would like to avoid an open-ended liability if possible.

If legal can propose tight language that limits scope of "unlimited" exposure (e.g., narrow trigger, notice requirements, mitigation obligations, escrow/insurance offset), that'd be helpful. Also advise whether we can offer a royalty cap or escrow instead of removing the cap entirely.

Karthik — please confirm whether Digicorp is sensitive to any particular remedy (they've been consistent on "royalty or unlimited").

H

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carve-out maximum / evidence timing for IP indemnity

Hi all,

Thanks for flagging. Below are two practical negotiation positions (clean language) we can offer depending on sales appetite. Both aim to avoid unlimited exposure while responding to Digicorp's commercial needs.

Option A (Preferred for risk control):
- IP indemnity survives but is limited to (i) reasonable attorney fees and costs incurred in defense plus (ii) any amounts finally awarded to the claimant for infringement, provided Redwood's liability for such amounts is capped at $5,000,000 per claim and $10,000,000 aggregate.
- Redwood retains standard defenses (right to control defense, settlement without admission only with consent, etc.)
- Evidence preservation: Redwood agrees to preserve relevant system logs and KV cache snapshots for 90 days following notice; Digicorp to provide as much factual detail and sample prompts as available within 30 days.
- Equitable relief: parties agree that injunctive relief is available but financial remedies remain capped as above (no separate unlimited monetary bucket).

Option B (Compromise to move deal):
- IP indemnity excluded from monetary cap but expressly limited to (i) direct damages for third-party IP claims and (ii) capped royalty-style remedy equal to 2% of net fees paid to Redwood attributable to the accused product over a rolling 12-month period, with an overall monetary backstop at $20,000,000.
- Evidence preservation: Redwood to make available compressed logs and diagnostics on request within 14 days; formal preservation of raw KV cache requires subpoena/compelled process subject to lawful access.
- Injunctive relief: carve-out for equitable relief for claims seeking to enjoin alleged ongoing infringement; parties will meet to define interim process for expedited injunctive requests.

Notes: both options require a tighter notice and cooperation clause (we should add 10-day cure for minor misconfigurations and mitigation obligations). Option A is better for risk; Option B likely gets the signature quicker if sales needs pace.

If you want, I can draft redline snippets for Option B (sales-friendly) and Option A (legal-friendly).

-marissa

Attachment: Redwood_IP_Indemnity_Options_snippet.txt (draft snippets)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie@digicorp.com>
Cc: contracts@digicorp.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out maximum / evidence timing for IP indemnity

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. We appreciate the urgency.

After internal review, Redwood can proceed on a targeted compromise to get you to signature quickly while protecting against open-ended exposure. Proposed (clean) language below — this is our formal counter.

Proposed counter (summary):
- IP indemnity: Redwood will indemnify Digicorp for third-party claims of IP infringement where (i) Digicorp provides prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation, and (ii) Redwood has the right to defend. Monetary remedies for such claims will be excluded from the standard MSA monetary cap but limited to the greater of (a) amounts finally awarded to the claimant and (b) a royalty-style remediation equal to 2% of net fees paid by Digicorp to Redwood attributable to the accused use during the prior 12 months, subject to a per-claim backstop of $15,000,000 and an aggregate cap of $30,000,000.
- Evidence and timing: Digicorp must provide initial written notice and summary of accused use within 30 days of becoming aware. Redwood will preserve relevant application logs and compressed KV snapshots for 90 days after notice and will provide export of logs within 14 days of request. Parties will meet to define additional preservation mechanics for raw data subject to lawful process.
- Equitable relief: The parties agree that injunctive relief is available and not subject to the monetary caps described above; however, parties will first attempt expedited discussions and agree to use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid serial injunctive filings.

We are willing to accept Digicorp's suggested 30-day initial notice window and the 90-day preservation period, and to make the monetary exclusion with the royalty-backing and backstops noted above. Our goal is to balance Digicorp's need for a meaningful remedy with predictability on Redwood's side.

If that's acceptable in principle, Karthik (sales) can route this into the order form and we can send an updated MSA + order form with the revised language for signature.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_IP_Clause_2028-04-15.txt (clean counter)

From: Natalie Park <natalie@digicorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@digicorp.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out maximum / evidence timing for IP indemnity

Hannah — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. We reviewed the proposed counter with counsel. The royalty-backed exclusion with the $15M per-claim / $30M aggregate backstop is acceptable to Digicorp provided: 1) the 14-day log export commitment is in the MSA (not a separate side letter); and 2) the parties add a brief clause that Digicorp may seek preliminary injunctive relief without having to exhaust expedited discussions if there is a credible imminent risk of continued infringement.

Please send the updated MSA + order form reflecting the language and we'll prepare signatures. I've attached our updated order form for your reference with the routing and AR contacts.

Thanks,
Natalie Park
Senior Contracts Manager — Digicorp
